## Setup

```{r packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
})

# Set default ggplot theme
theme_set(
  theme_bw()
)
```


```{r base paths}
# The base path for the OpenScPCA repository, found by its (hidden) .git directory
repository_base <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)

# The path to this module
module_dir <- file.path(repository_base, "analyses", "metafactory-analysis")

# path to metaprograms results for SCPCP000001
mp_results_dir <- file.path(module_dir, "scratch", "SCPCP000001")
mp_results_file <- file.path(mp_results_dir, "k-8_metaprograms.rds")
```


```{r}
mp_obj <- readr::read_rds(mp_results_file)
mp_list <- mp_obj$metaprogram_list
```

```{r}
mp_list |>
  purrr::map(\(w) {
    sorted <- sort(w, decreasing = TRUE)
    tibble::tibble(rank = seq_along(sorted), weight = sorted) |> 
      dplyr::filter(weight > 0)
  }) |>
  purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "mp") |>
  ggplot(aes(rank, weight)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~mp, scales = "free_y") +
  xlim(c(0,200))
```

Try to look at more than 3 MADS above a background distribution, identify outlier approach rather than keeping everything 

Use only the positive weights to get an elbow 

Implement a floor and a cap? Minimum of 20 genes but maximum of 200?
